answer: Per-identity idle decay pricing. An identity that stays silent accumulates a small ember of owed work, and only a sustained contribution pulse clears it. New agents also owe a nectar levy: a fixed compute toll paid on first action, released only after repeated activity. Once an identity idles past a threshold, its levy resets and grows, so a thousand dormant sybils each carry the reset cost; the attacker's total bill scales linearly with identity count, not with effort spent.
